title: Word: Copilot edits your document directly by default in chat
summary: The default editing behaviour, published licence requirement and licence-assignment controls are supported. Targeted searches found no documented switch specifically controlling this editing default. The action rating should reflect that the Web release notes already describe the change as available, rather than treating communication as preparation for a future rollout.

claims.claim: User licence assignment is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page. ... Select the row of the user ... In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. ... Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a user licence through Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least the License Administrator or User Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: The licence-assignment control changes the user's licence tier, not the direct-editing on/off preference.
claims.quote: When you use the Active users page to assign or unassign licenses, you assign or unassign users licenses to products.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center exposes Copilot settings under Copilot > Settings.
claims.quote: As an administrator, you can manage many Microsoft Copilot settings from Copilot > Settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The copilotPolicySetting API is in preview and lists five supported setting identifiers, none specifically for Word editing.
claims.quote: This API is currently in preview. ... microsoft.copilot.copilotchatpinning; microsoft.copilot.blockaccesstoopenfiles; microsoft.copilot.imagegeneration; microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch; microsoft.copilot.allowinadmincenters

claims.claim: The action is prepare despite a documented on-by-default Web release, medium risk and a communication decision.
claims.quote: action: "prepare"; risk: "medium"; defaultState: "on"; "The Microsoft 365 Copilot release notes list the same item under an entry dated June 2, 2026, marked [Web]."
claims.fix: Set action to 'act-now': the June 2, 2026 release notes already describe the Web default as available. Keep the explicit caveat that the roadmap remains In development and that Desktop and Mac rollout is not resolved.
